title: The probe census and the flake-harness result it ingests
$comment: The six ROOT definitions are `census_v1`, `census_v2`, `census_v3`, `census_v4`, `census_v5` and `flake_result_v1`; tools/probe_census.py maps each declared schema string to one of them. They are deliberately not named after the schema strings themselves, because a JSON Pointer treats `/` as a separator and `#/$defs/probe-census/v2` would name nothing.
description: The declared shape of every document tools/probe_census.py reads or writes (#1492). It replaces hand-rolled type, presence, closed-object, enum, length and range checking; it deliberately declares NO cross-field invariant -- those span fields, so no keyword expresses them and they live in tools/probe_census.py's census_invariants()/result_invariants() (#1493) -- and no parity with the live probe registry, which stays validate_manifest's report and --seed's repair. Every object here is closed: explicit `required` plus `additionalProperties: false`, with a nullable field REQUIRED and null-inclusive rather than optional, so deleting one is a violation rather than an absence. Enums are spelled as one-element `enum` rather than `const` on purpose: the library's const message names only the value it EXPECTED, while enum names the offending one.

census_v1.$comment: #1425's seed: the inventory alone, with no census record. Declared so --seed can validate what it migrates FROM, and so a stored v1 census is reported as schema drift rather than as corruption.

census_v2.$comment: #1428's record: the same inventory, each row carrying its census. FROZEN at the six-field record, because this is now a migration INPUT: it must keep describing what a stored v2 census actually looks like, so `--seed` can validate the document it migrates from. Pointing it at the current `inventory_row` would make every real v2 census invalid for carrying no `claims`, which is the one thing migration exists to add.

census_v3.$comment: #1434's record: the v2 document with each row's census also carrying its append-only `claims` log. Claim acquisitions are a DEDICATED collection rather than more `attempts`, which tools/probe_census.py defines as result-ingestion attempts and deliberately makes non-idempotent. FROZEN for the same reason census_v2 is: it is now a migration INPUT, and pointing it at the current row would make every real v3 census invalid for carrying no `outcomes`.

census_v4.$comment: #1439's record: the v3 document with each row's census also carrying its append-only `outcomes` log. Frozen as migration input now that v5 adds deferral state.

census_v5.$comment: The v4 document with first-class per-probe deferral state. A deferred probe remains registered and keeps all measurement history, but the de-flake selector excludes it until a maintainer explicitly resumes it.

inventory_row_v2.$comment: A stored v2 row. Frozen alongside census_v2 and never widened.

inventory_row_v3.$comment: A stored v3 row. Frozen alongside census_v3 and never widened.

inventory_row_v4.$comment: A stored v4 row. Frozen alongside census_v4 and never widened.

census_record_v2.$comment: A stored v2 record: the six fields #1428 wrote, with no `claims`. Frozen -- it describes migration INPUT, so widening it would make every real v2 census invalid.

acceptable_failures.$comment: X (#1430): the failures a complete 10-run measurement may show and still be acceptable, so 0 through 9 -- an X of 10 would declare a probe that never passes acceptable. Still null-INCLUSIVE here, and only here: a census written before the policy existed holds nulls, and tools/probe_census.py's --seed has to be able to read one in order to initialize it to 0. policy_invariants() is what refuses a null on every candidate and on --validate.

estimated_worst_case_seconds.$comment: Supplied metadata, distinct from a sample's OBSERVED worst_elapsed_seconds.

current.$comment: The current commit cohort, or null when nothing has been measured. Spelled as if/else rather than oneOf so a malformed cohort reports the field that is actually wrong instead of `is not valid under any of the given schemas`.

census_record_v3.$comment: A stored v3 record: the seven fields #1434 left behind, with no `outcomes`. Frozen -- it describes migration INPUT, so widening it would make every real v3 census invalid.

census_record.$comment: Exactly the nine fields probe_census.empty_census() writes.

claims.$comment: #1434's append-only log of successful claim ACQUISITIONS, keyed for idempotency by `token`. Deliberately not `attempts`, which are result-ingestion attempts and are non-idempotent by design.

outcomes.$comment: #1439's append-only log of a de-flake attempt's STABLE NON-SUCCESS outcomes, keyed for idempotency by `attempt`. A repair that passed its gate is not here: it becomes a pull request, not a census row.

deferred.$comment: Null when selectable. Otherwise the maintainer decision that temporarily removes this probe from de-flake selection without deleting it, changing CI classification, or discarding measurements.

claim.$comment: Exactly what probe_claim_lease.Claim.census_record() writes: one successful acquisition of the per-probe lock, recorded BEFORE the measurement it authorizes runs. `token` is the acquisition token and the idempotency key -- replaying the same acquisition must remain one record, and the same token carrying different metadata is refused rather than appended.

pid.$comment: NOT `count`: a pid is not a tally and legitimately exceeds that definition's million -- Linux allows a pid_max up to 2^22.

outcome.$comment: One de-flake attempt's ending, written by exactly two workflows: deflake_outcome.outcome_record() for the three STABLE NON-SUCCESS outcomes (#1439), and deflake_issue.outcome_record() for the production-defect one it files a tracker issue for (#1438). ONE shape, because one `outcomes` collection holds every ending and a reader must not have to know which workflow wrote each entry. `attempt` is the attempt identity and the idempotency key -- resuming an already-recorded attempt must remain one record, and the same identity carrying different evidence is refused rather than appended. The record is a RESUME point: it carries the summarized measurement evidence, artifact REFERENCES and the diagnostic summary, so a later reader never has to re-run the attempt to know what it established.

The three STABLE outcomes (#1439) and the filed production defect (#1438). An operational error is deliberately not one of them: exit codes 2-4, an incomplete run set and malformed measurement data return an actionable non-success and record nothing at all. `production-defect` is spelled as #1437's own route identifier, because that ending IS the route it was handed -- two vocabularies for one concept is how a census row stops being greppable against the diagnosis that produced it.

reason.$comment: WHY #1437 took the route this outcome answers, in its own machine-readable vocabulary (deflake_diagnosis.REASONS). `outcome` says what was concluded; this says what the invocation actually established. A `cannot-reproduce` whose condition could not be recreated carries no de-list recommendation precisely because of this field. Deliberately NOT enumerated here: the vocabulary is tools/deflake_diagnosis.py's and grows with its routes, and a second copy in a data file would be the one that went stale.

probe.$comment: Redundant with the row key, and required anyway: an outcome record is handed BETWEEN workflows, so it has to name its own probe. probe_census.ingest_outcome refuses one that disagrees with the row it is being appended to.

configuration.$comment: The gitignored config/*.local.yaml manifest both controlled batches read, as tools/deflake.py records it. An EMPTY list is the expected default and a real statement -- every member of the family absent -- so the KEY is required and the entries are not.

summary.$comment: The diagnostic or attempted-fix summary that explains the selected outcome. Prose, and required non-empty: an outcome nobody can read is not a resume point.

recommendation.$comment: ADVISORY ONLY, and only ever on cannot-reproduce. Nothing reads this to change tools/ci_probes.py: de-listing is a person's decision, and every independent non-flaky exclusion reason survives it.

comparison.$comment: Only ever on partial-improvement: the before-and-after failure counts, the X-out-of-N ceiling they are judged against, and the acceptance condition that stayed unmet.

issue.$comment: The tracker issue a production defect was filed as (#1438). OPTIONAL rather than nullable-and-required, because #1439's three stable outcomes were written before this key existed and a stored one carries no `issue` at all; the allOf below is what makes it REQUIRED on a production-defect and FORBIDDEN on the other three, so absence is never an accident either way.

allOf.$comment: A filed production defect names the issue it was filed as. Without this the ending could be recorded with no way back to the human-reviewed lane it exists to enter, which is the whole outcome.

outcome_issue.$comment: Exactly what deflake_issue.require_issue_identity() stores: the tracker issue this attempt was filed as, the STABLE publication key it was filed under, and the issue-origin brand the canonical review gate routes on. The key is what a resume reconciles against the tracker, so an issue created before a crash is reused rather than duplicated; it is DERIVED from the handoff, never supplied by a caller. `origin` IS enumerated here, unlike the sibling `reason` field: that vocabulary is tools/deflake_diagnosis.py's and grows with its routes, while this one is the closed pair approve_issues.py's own ORIGIN_RE matches, and tools/test_deflake_diagnosis.py holds the two spellings to each other.

outcome_invocation.$comment: WHICH /deflake invocation the diagnosis consumed: the exact command and the directory it ran in. The census row cannot answer this -- probe_census.ingest_result drops the command and the invocation directory -- so an outcome record that did not keep it could not say what was actually run.

advisory.$comment: Always true. Spelled as a stored field rather than left implicit so a reader of the raw census cannot mistake the recommendation for an applied change.

unmet_condition.$comment: DERIVED from the diagnosis outcome's own `reason`, never text a caller supplies. It repeats the record's top-level `reason` on purpose: `comparison` is the self-contained evidence for the numeric claim, and a reader of it alone must be able to see which acceptance condition stayed unmet.

outcome_measurement.$comment: One measurement the outcome rests on, summarized from its own probe-flake-result/v1 document. References, never copies: retained_artifacts are the paths probe_flake kept OUTSIDE every worktree, and no stdout, protocol stream or engine log enters the census.

exit_code.$comment: The tools/probe_flake.py exit the measurement came back with: 0 a valid measurement, 2 a rejection before execution, 3 port exhaustion, 4 an untrustworthy harness result. 2 and 3 write no document at all; 4 writes one whose own status says harness-error.

error_run_index.$comment: The index of the run whose stream could not be trusted, or null. Its own field because probe_flake keeps that run OUT of `runs`, so an all-PASS `runs` list is not on its own evidence of a trustworthy measurement.

outcome_run.$comment: One run's durable outcome. The per-run check map stays in the retained artifacts; check_counts is the tally the outcome is judged on.

outcome_census_reference.$comment: The coordinates that address this measurement in the census: a probe row's cohort is keyed by commit and each of its samples by timestamp, so the pair locates the stored sample when one exists. It is deliberately a REFERENCE and not an assertion that the sample is stored -- only the #1436 measurement is ingested by --record, while a controlled comparison batch is evidence that lives in its retained artifact tree, and a reference that claimed otherwise would be inventing a census row.

cohort.$comment: One commit's accumulated samples. Append-only; the writer never rewrites one.

sample.$comment: Exactly what probe_census.summarize_sample() keeps: summarized outcomes and artifact REFERENCES. Every producer-only field is absent by closure, not by an exclusion list.

sample_run.$comment: One run as the census keeps it: the producer's `port` and per-run `checks` map are dropped.

attempt.$comment: Exactly what probe_census.summarize_attempt() keeps: one well-formed ingestion attempt, accepted or not.

flake_result_v1.$comment: The INGESTION document, exactly as probe_flake.Measurement.to_document() writes it. Declared here rather than in tools/probe_flake.py, which is out of scope for #1492: this is the consumer's intake contract.

error_run.$comment: The one run whose protocol stream could not be trusted, or null. Never a member of `runs`, and never a fourth probe outcome. if/else for the same reason as `current`.

checks.$comment: The probe's own check descriptor: ordered id/label pairs.

result_run.$comment: One valid run of the harness. `checks` is the per-run check map; declaring it an OBJECT is what refuses the truthy non-dict that used to raise AttributeError.

harness_error_run.$comment: Structurally a run, but carrying the one outcome `runs` may never hold.

run_checks.$comment: check id -> that run's result for it.

check_counts.$comment: check id -> its PASS/FAIL/MISSING tally across the measurement.

protocol_status.$comment: probe_flake.protocol_status()'s two answers today. A future probe-result version is a deliberate edit here, not something to leave open.

run_outcome.$comment: The three outcomes a VALID run may report. HARNESS_ERROR is not one: it labels error_run alone.

commit_sha.$comment: A 40-hex commit, or the literal `unknown` probe_flake records when git could not be consulted.

capabilities.$comment: RTS capabilities and peak concurrency. Positive is what the producer guarantees: probe_flake refuses --rts-caps below 1 and --runs below 1, and the concurrency registry floors its own count at 1.
